items.front: Which two southern dynasties dominate the post-Gupta Deccan/South, and their capitals?
items.back: Pallavas (capital Kanchipuram) and Chalukyas of Badami (capital Vatapi/Badami) — long-time rivals.
items.examPoint: Emergence of the Pallavas — Simhavishnu, Kalabhras & Kanchi capital
items.source: APPSC GK — Pallavas & Chalukyas

items.front: Who founded the imperial Pallavas and whom did he defeat?
items.back: Simhavishnu (575–590 CE); defeated the Kalabhras; patron of the poet Bharavi (Kiratarjuniya).
items.examPoint: Simhavishnu — founder, Avanisimha, patron of Bharavi (Kiratarjuniya)
items.source: APPSC GK — Pallavas & Chalukyas

items.front: Mahendravarman I — his book, art innovation, and defeat?
items.back: Wrote Mattavilasa Prahasana; began rock-cut (Mahendra) temples; defeated by Pulakeshin II at the Battle of Pullalur.
items.examPoint: Mahendravarman I — Mattavilasa Prahasana, Chitrakarapuli, Mahendra rock-cut style, Pullalur
items.source: APPSC GK — Pallavas & Chalukyas

items.front: Narasimhavarman I 'Mamalla' — title, big victory, monuments?
items.back: Title Vatapikonda; defeated Pulakeshin II & razed Vatapi; founded Mamallapuram + the Seven Rathas; hosted Hsuen Tsang (642 CE).
items.examPoint: Narasimhavarman I (Mamalla) — Vatapikonda, destroyed Vatapi, Mahabalipuram/Seven Rathas, Sri Lanka, Hsuen Tsang
items.source: APPSC GK — Pallavas & Chalukyas

items.front: Which Pallava built the Shore Temple and the Kailashnath Temple?
items.back: Narasimhavarman II (Rajasimha, 695–722 CE) — structural Rajasimha style; also sent embassies to China.
items.examPoint: Narasimhavarman II (Rajasimha) — Shore Temple, Kailashnath Temple, embassies to China
items.source: APPSC GK — Pallavas & Chalukyas

items.front: Nandivarman II — his temple and its deity?
items.back: Built the Vaikunth Perumal Temple at Kanchi (dedicated to Vishnu); promoted Bhakti & village autonomy.
items.examPoint: Nandivarman II — Vaikunth Perumal Temple, Bhakti, village autonomy
items.source: APPSC GK — Pallavas & Chalukyas

items.front: The four Pallava architectural styles in order?
items.back: Mahendra (rock-cut caves) → Mamalla (monolithic Rathas) → Rajasimha (structural temples) → Nandivarman (smaller/decline).
items.examPoint: Pallava architectural styles (Mahendra, Mamalla, Rajasimha, Nandivarman)
items.source: APPSC GK — Pallavas & Chalukyas

items.front: Shore Temple vs Seven Rathas — who built which?
items.back: Seven Rathas (monolithic) = Narasimhavarman I; Shore Temple + Kailashnath (structural) = Narasimhavarman II. Both at/near Mamallapuram.
items.examPoint: Major Pallava temples & monuments (Shore, Kailashnath, Seven Rathas, Vaikunth Perumal)
items.source: APPSC GK — Pallavas & Chalukyas

items.front: Pallava village assemblies and village court?
items.back: Sabha (Brahmadeya villages) and Urar (ordinary villages); court = Dharmasasana; realm divided into Kottams.
items.examPoint: Pallava administration — Kottams, Sabha/Urar, Dharmasasana, Dharma-Maharaja
items.source: APPSC GK — Pallavas & Chalukyas

items.front: Pallava economy terms: Brahmadeya, Manigramam, Eripatti?
items.back: Brahmadeya = tax-free land to Brahmins; Manigramam = merchant guild; Eripatti = tank land funding village tanks.
items.examPoint: Pallava economy — land revenue, Brahmadeya, Manigramam, Eripatti, coinage
items.source: APPSC GK — Pallavas & Chalukyas

items.front: The Bhakti saints of the Pallava era?
items.back: Alvars (devotees of Vishnu) and Nayanars (devotees of Shiva); Adi Shankaracharya reinforced Advaita.
items.examPoint: Society & religion — Saivism/Vaishnavism, Alvars & Nayanars, Adi Shankaracharya
items.source: APPSC GK — Pallavas & Chalukyas

items.front: How did Pallava rule end?
items.back: The last Pallava, Aparajitavarman, was defeated by the Chola king Aditya I (late 9th c. CE) → rise of the Cholas.
items.examPoint: Decline of the Pallavas — Aparajitavarman defeated by Aditya I (Cholas)
items.source: APPSC GK — Pallavas & Chalukyas

items.front: Chalukyas of Badami — founder and greatest king?
items.back: Founder Pulakeshin I (fortified Vatapi, did Ashvamedha); greatest = Pulakeshin II, who checked Harsha on the Narmada.
items.examPoint: Pulakeshin II — greatest Chalukya, checked Harsha on the Narmada, defeated by Narasimhavarman I
items.source: APPSC GK — Pallavas & Chalukyas

items.front: Aihole inscription — author, temple, what it records?
items.back: Prashasti by Jain court poet Ravikirti; on the Meguti Jain temple (634 CE); records Pulakeshin II's victories incl. checking Harsha.
items.examPoint: Aihole inscription of Ravikirti (Meguti temple prashasti)
items.source: APPSC GK — Pallavas & Chalukyas

items.front: Pulakeshin II's foreign contact; Chalukya architecture centres?
items.back: Exchanged embassies with Sasanian Khusrau II (Ajanta Cave 1 mural); temples at Badami, Aihole ('cradle') & Pattadakal (UNESCO); Vesara style.
items.examPoint: Pulakeshin II diplomacy & Chalukya administration — Sasanian embassy, navy, centralisation
items.source: Aihole inscription; Ajanta; APPSC GK — Pallavas & Chalukyas

items.front: Pallava core region?
items.back: South Andhra Pradesh and north Tamil Nadu, ruled from Kanchipuram.
